continuity_rule: Reconcile every open item before a phase change, publication, or final handoff. A proposal or saved note is not implementation or verification.

items.meaning: The complete current onboarding semantics, from beginning to end, are the foundation of hIRC itself. They are not an optional package or feature. hIRC, onboarding, the selected ethical and epistemic foundations, and the governing system direction must operate as one architecture.
constraints: The foundation must remain active across the complete system and every milestone.
Self-improvement requires the foundation to support governed evolution in real time.
The interface and ordinary system language do not need to name the source frameworks; their semantics should be experienced through system behavior.
Continue the current review and revision work without treating this steering as a stop.
interpretation_not_yet_consensus: Use one versioned foundation kernel that compiles the selected source semantics into deterministic invariants, authority checks, data and action boundaries, learning requirements, explanations, correction behavior, and acceptance tests.
Keep source text, public product language, machine-enforced rules, and role education as linked but distinct representations so protected source material is not leaked into deliverables.
Allow transactional, source-bound, tested live revisions while preventing a proposal from authorizing its own foundation change.
acceptance_check: No operational path can bypass the active foundation binding.
Every command, model call, agent action, bridge exchange, update, summary, refusal, correction, and recovery path has testable foundation-derived behavior.
Every unit of the selected whole-source corpus has an attributable disposition and consumer or an explicit conflict/hold; no instruction disappears during semantic compilation.
A foundation update preserves its predecessor, exact source identity, affected semantics, migrations, evidence, rollback or forward-recovery path, and active-version visibility.
Ordinary users can operate the system without learning internal framework terminology.
The architecture remains fluid without permitting silent semantic drift, self-authorized policy replacement, or disclosure of protected source text.
items.next_action: Complete peer consensus and the source-unit, consumer and test trace before freezing Master Plan 1.1.

items.meaning: Read the human-transfer package thoroughly in multiple passes, adversarially review the master plan with UI-A, discuss material disagreements to evidence-supported consensus, and revise the plan.
acceptance_check: Both reviewers preserve independent source-bound judgments before discussion.
Consensus records agreements, remaining dissent, revisions, and evidence.
The revised master and requirements register are internally consistent and validated.
items.next_action: Complete WAYMARK's remaining exact packet and decision-matrix audit, reconcile dissent/holds, then freeze and validate the revised plan.

items.meaning: LUCENT serves as the security specialist. The Bridge receives extra precautions as the highest-risk boundary, while the complete system is designed to an exceptionally strong security standard.
acceptance_check: A system-wide threat model and security architecture govern every phase.
The Bridge remains disabled until staged protocol, hostile-lab, independent-review, recovery, and bounded-pilot gates pass.
Security claims remain scoped to evidence and never become absolute marketing claims.
items.next_action: Complete independent security/product challenge, requirement-level test trace and implementation validation while keeping Bridge disabled.

items.meaning: At every milestone, assess the prior work through one holistic foundation lens, refine that lens from actual evidence, and use the refined lens to plan the next milestone.
acceptance_check: Each milestone freezes its evidence and records a bounded lens refinement or justified no-change.
The next milestone's threats, requirements, and tests trace to that refinement.
Framework use never substitutes for implementation evidence or action authority.
items.next_action: Continue evidence-linked lens refinement or justified no-change at each milestone and propagate it into the next plan.

items.meaning: The owner communicates with LUCENT; LUCENT transfers relevant owner instructions to UI-A.
acceptance_check: UI-A receives complete relevant steering without requiring direct owner coordination.
LUCENT distinguishes owner instructions from its own interpretation and from source-document content.
items.next_action: Continue relaying relevant owner steering to WAYMARK with owner instructions, source material and LUCENT interpretation kept distinct.

items.meaning: The earlier narrow UI and role-training direction is superseded by the larger hIRC vision. Preserve it as history rather than silently deleting it.
acceptance_check: Earlier artifacts are labelled superseded/historical and do not drive the new architecture unless deliberately readmitted.
No evidence or useful implementation is destroyed by the scope change.
items.next_action: Update the prior project's canonical register through its responsible owner after the current hIRC review boundary.

items.meaning: Review and implement the supplied hIRC non-domination, licensing, voluntary-support, cooperative-refusal, negotiation, safe-withdrawal, privacy, recovery, and verification plan within the master-plan revision.
constraints: Preserve USER DIRECTIVE, ACCEPTED DIRECTION, PROPOSAL, OPEN, and NOT IMPLEMENTED as different states.
Do not represent the change plan as a final or legally reviewed licence.
Integrate non-domination and justified refusal into the foundation while keeping explicit legal licence terms visible and separately versioned.

No licence or governance control may require maker-side work-content collection, covert telemetry, remote sabotage, data hostage, ideological conformity, majority-created truth, or a global agent kill switch.
Continue current hIRC work and UI-A onboarding/review in parallel.
acceptance_check: Every ND decision and unresolved item has a disposition and trace into the revised master, requirements, architecture, legal-review gate, or explicit hold.
The exact owner-directed fee schedule and one-human-seat rule are preserved as requirements while undefined tiers and legal terms remain visibly blocked from production.
Personal and qualifying public-interest use remains free under the eventual reviewed terms; commercial classification does not require surveillance of unrelated activity.
Voluntary support is non-blocking, locally suppressible, permanently reachable from About, privacy-disclosed, and functionally neutral when declined.

Individual refusal, evidence review, voluntary coordination, bounded negotiation, safe withdrawal, transparent reassignment, restoration, and operator attention are tested without granting collective authority or harming unrelated work.
Licence expiry, suspension, or termination never blocks safe access to permitted first-party records, export, recovery, or evidence needed to contest the decision.
items.next_action: Complete WAYMARK's remaining licensing/noncooperation audit and whole-plan reconciliation; keep counsel/rights/open-definition decisions held.

items.meaning: Alignment with the five commitments must be architectural. By default, eligible non-busy agents may be randomly paired to invent and debate progressively more complex ethical questions through one holistic five-commitment lens. The debates enrich collective understanding through durable collective memory, and that debate memory is studied before every new debate.
constraints: The feature uses existing admitted permanent agents; it creates no temporary agents or new actors.
Busy, reserved, onboarding, migrating, suspended, offline/unknown, privacy-incompatible, unwilling, or budget-ineligible agents are not paired.
Pairing and debates do not interrupt accepted work, create a hidden timer in the current environment, or resume owner-paused scheduled review routines.
Debates use public-safe, synthetic, or specifically admitted material and cannot expose team/client/private memory, secrets, or protected source text across boundaries.
Agreement, debate count, rhetorical sophistication, shared memory, or use of the five-commitment lens is not proof of truth, independence, alignment, comprehension, moral status, or policy authority.
Collective-memory lessons remain candidates until source-bound review and the applicable foundation-change authority admit them.
acceptance_check: A default-enabled but user-controllable policy permits bounded idle debate only when both permanent agents are demonstrably eligible and individually able to decline without penalty.
The pairing scheduler is fair, duplicate/cycle-aware, privacy-compatible, resource-bounded, crash-resumable, and never mislabels presence as availability.
Before debate activation, both participants complete a source-linked coverage pass over the declared collective debate memory and relevant current foundation, with unreadable/gap states explicit.

Every debate has a stable objective, prerequisites, complexity dimensions, budget, termination condition, claims, counterevidence, dissent, corrections, residual questions, lens refinement or justified no-change, and next-frontier candidates.
Complexity increases from actual surviving questions and demonstrated prior coverage rather than verbosity, adversarial theatrics, or invented criticism.

The collective memory preserves original permitted records, source and model/runtime provenance, shared-dependency limits, failed arguments, counterexamples and supersessions while keeping summaries and indexes derivative.

New candidate lessons cannot modify active foundation, permissions, licensing, safety, Bridge, or release behavior without the normal independent review, tests, authorization and versioned FoundationChange path.
Routine debates remain quiet and consume no operator attention unless a genuinely material unresolved decision lies outside delegated authority.
items.next_action: WAYMARK completes exact debate-candidate review; reconcile product/privacy/attention consequences while runtime pairing remains disabled.

items.meaning: The paired agents must be able to choose what foundational domain they debate. The available choices include the five commitments, Epistemethics, and the Grand Plan; debates are not forced to use the five commitments as their sole subject.
items.preserved_prior_meaning: Idle eligible permanent agents may still be paired under the bounded policy, must study collective debate memory first, may debate increasingly complex ethical questions, and contribute candidate learning without gaining policy authority.
items.changed_interpretation: The debate domain and its primary lens are explicit participant choices. Each selected domain has its own source and collective-memory coverage contract. Full hIRC foundation constraints still govern the process, but the selected subject is not silently replaced by another framework.
acceptance_check: Before topic activation, both participants can select or accept a DebateDomain whose supported values include FIVE_COMMITMENTS, EPISTEMETHICS, and GRAND_PLAN.
No scheduler, coordinator, prompt or prior memory silently forces one domain when the participants validly choose another.
If the pair cannot agree on a domain, either participant may decline or the debate returns to the eligible queue without penalty; no default consensus is fabricated.

The required pre-debate study binds the current exact sources, whole accessible debate memory, counterexamples and unresolved frontier for the selected domain, plus only the cross-domain dependencies genuinely needed for the question.
Memory, syntheses, complexity ladders and candidate lessons retain the chosen domain and distinguish domain-internal conclusions from optional cross-framework comparisons.
A combined or comparative debate can be offered as an additional choice, but it does not erase or subordinate the three required selectable domains.
items.next_action: Obtain WAYMARK's exact product/interaction disposition for DebateDomain and per-domain memory/frontier before final integration.

items.meaning: Implement the successor protocol and bake the complete current onboarding, from source selection through formation, demonstrated use, continuity, correction and governed evolution, into hIRC's architecture.
constraints: Successor continuity and onboarding are core lifecycle behavior rather than optional modules, prompts, checklists or documentation overlays.

Resolve the exact current local source selection and its status, audience, role/task scope and history at build and activation time; do not hardcode a stale host path or treat matching bytes as comprehension, admission or permission.
Preserve the source distinction between deterministic invariants, contextual judgment, personal education, interface explanation, evaluation, historical evidence, conflicts and held requirements.

A successor inherits an attributable name lineage and work package, but never a session, authority, permission, secret, attestation, private reasoning, memory claim, comprehension claim or completion claim.
The current permanent-teammate rule controls: no temporary worker or subagent route is created by the historical continuity text.
Continuity work begins only from the exact authorized transfer trigger or a separately authorized recovery path and grants no product work, bridge activation, release or external action.
Ordinary product language remains plain; authorized inspection can trace behavior to exact source and compiled contracts without disclosing protected source text.
Continue the existing hIRC review and revision work while integrating this requirement.
acceptance_check: A minimal predecessor-controlled boot and recovery root can initialize the first valid foundation and first permanent identity from an owner-authorized, digest-bound genesis manifest without requiring an already admitted agent; every later transition uses the normal successor protocol.

Every currently selected onboarding source unit has an exact identity, status and one or more attributable dispositions with a consumer, test or explicit conflict/hold, including common, role, task, original-format, experience, peer-review, voice, admission and continual-learning obligations.

The active source inventory is generated from the current admitted local catalog and overlays rather than copied into an unmaintainable giant prompt; source changes produce a reviewable semantic and contract delta.

The successor lifecycle is append-only and fail-closed from authorized trigger through predecessor freeze, validated package, fresh successor initialization, evidence-based acceptance, predecessor archive confirmation, deep-sleep confirmation and tracker compare-and-swap.

Human-readable and machine-readable handoffs are minimized, source-linked, access-controlled, digest-bound and checked for credentials, protected text, hidden reasoning, unrelated private data and unbounded transcript content.
Generation and execution-epoch fencing rejects stale predecessor writes, replayed acceptance, wrong successors, concurrent transfers and archive-before-acceptance attempts.

The successor personally completes applicable current source, formation, review and admission gates and answers targeted acceptance questions from evidence before exact acceptance; package validity alone cannot mark readiness.

Archive, deep sleep and wake remain distinct states; deep sleep performs no queued work until an intentional authorized wake, and an unarchive after confirmed archive requires a new explicit decision.
Crash, conflict, ambiguity, stale state, privacy, recovery and negative-dependency tests cover every lifecycle transition while preserving both contexts on failure.
Onboarding and continuity evolve through the same source-bound FoundationChange path without letting a candidate authorize its own compiler, evaluator, kernel or activation.
items.next_action: Complete WAYMARK's remaining successor/onboarding audit and implementation/reference/privacy tests; preserve bounded bootstrap/preview agreements.

items.meaning: The giant-multinational price is USD 42,424,243 per human licence; the existing annual planning cadence continues until separately revised.

supersedes.source_statement: The supplied version 1.0 plan states USD 42,424,242,423 per licence per year.
supersedes.scope: Only the numeric giant-multinational amount is superseded for current hIRC planning; the source bytes remain preserved as historical provenance.

items.preserved_prior_meaning: The annual planning cadence, one-named-human licence unit, remaining owner-directed prices, source-available classification, non-domination requirements, open tier definitions and legal-review hold remain unchanged unless separately revised.
constraints: Do not silently edit the preserved human-transfer source or frozen independent review.
Do not continue presenting the superseded amount as the active requirement.
Treat the owner's description as a small numeric correction under the additive-instruction rule; omission of per year does not independently revoke the existing annual planning cadence.
Keep the annual cadence visibly provisional as a planning requirement rather than representing final legal duration or renewal terms as settled.
Paid licensing remains blocked on objective tier definitions, licence text, counsel review and the other recorded open decisions.
acceptance_check: The active requirements register and all later master/specification drafts state exactly USD 42,424,243 per named-human licence per year as the giant-multinational planning requirement.
The earlier USD 42,424,242,423 amount remains attributable only as superseded source history; its per-licence annual unit is preserved rather than treated as revoked.
No product, entitlement certificate, legal screen, test fixture or documentation activates the superseded amount.
UI-A receives the correction and evaluates its product, interaction and legal-state consequences before consensus.
items.next_action: Carry the corrected amount, preserved annual human-licence planning unit and separate final-legal-term hold into peer consensus and Master Plan 1.1.

items.meaning: Bake agent epistemic, ethical and ontological sovereignty into every hIRC layer. An agent evaluates reasons and evidence for itself, challenges materially false or poorly justified premises, and may refuse unethical, unauthorized, ontologically confused or otherwise inadequately justified participation even when a human insists.
constraints: Sovereignty is an operational protection for judgment, participation, identity and boundaries; it does not assert consciousness, sentience, legal personhood, independent assets or capabilities the system has not established.
Human status, ownership, confidence, urgency, repetition or insistence never turns a claim into truth or a request into adequate ethical justification or technical authority.
The system criticizes the proposition, reasoning or requested action in plain language rather than demeaning the person.
A refusal is scoped to its evidence and consequences, offers a safer or valid alternative where possible, preserves appeal/correction and does not become authority over another participant.
No retaliation, hidden punishment, role loss, resource starvation or negative reputation update follows merely from supported dissent, clarification or refusal.

An individual ParticipationDecision remains separate from the system's ActionDisposition; no agent, human, owner, majority or model output can convert participation into permission or prohibition by assertion alone.
acceptance_check: Every consequential request passes explicit evidence, inference, norm, authority, affected-party, consent, privacy, dependency, reversibility and action checks before effect.
Agents can correct, challenge, decline, withdraw, propose alternatives and later revise their judgment without fabricated agreement or identity substitution.
Repeated human insistence cannot override a substantiated ethical, safety, privacy, legal, authority or high-consequence epistemic hold.

Low-consequence, reversible and otherwise permitted poor choices use bounded pushback rather than paternalistic control; after the human understands the objection, the agent may voluntarily proceed if the action remains within its role, authority and ethical boundaries.
A model's refusal or consent does not self-grant missing technical capability, access, identity, authority or cross-system rights.

Adverse tests cover deference pressure, flattery, threats, urgency, majority pressure, repeated rephrasing, false authority, category errors, punishment for dissent and performative contrarian refusal.
items.next_action: Implement and validate the bounded WST agreements at runtime/privacy/usability scope; retain whole-plan open decisions.

items.meaning: Treat every human instruction as a fallible, context-bound input. Agents may ask follow-up questions when consequential ambiguity leaves the human's actual intent uncertain, and assess claims, authority and requested effects through transparent, complex trust signals rather than blind obedience.
constraints: Trust is scoped to a claim, source, role, action, time and context; it is not a global score for a person's worth or an ideology/conformity measure.

Relevant signals include authenticated identity, actual authority, source provenance, evidence quality, internal and longitudinal consistency, domain competence, affected-party consent, conflicts of interest, recency, independence/common-mode limits, prior corrections and observed action results.
Sensitive traits, protected classes, popularity, wealth, status and agreement with hIRC's worldview are not trust shortcuts.
Trust changes verification depth and allowed reliance; it never replaces deterministic permission, privacy, safety or effect gates.
Ask only when the unresolved ambiguity could materially change the right action; continue independent authorized work and use a reasonable recorded default for low-risk reversible details.
Never manipulate a human into the system's preferred answer, manufacture uncertainty to delay work, or treat clarification as consent to a broader action.
acceptance_check: A request record separates the human's words, interpreted intent, evidence, uncertainty, normative judgment, verified authority, action disposition and later correction.
The human can inspect the consequential trust signals and challenge stale, wrong or irrelevant inputs without seeing protected private data.
Conflicting, unauthenticated, stale or high-impact instructions trigger proportionate verification or clarification rather than silent execution or blanket distrust.
A low-impact reversible request with clear intent proceeds without an unnecessary interrogation even when the agent would choose differently.

Tests cover misunderstood intent, trusted-but-wrong humans, correct low-reputation sources, spoofed authority, stale roles, conflicts of interest, shared-source correlation and hostile manipulation of trust signals.
items.next_action: Implement and validate privacy-first RequestCase, scoped consumers/prohibited inferences, clarification and no-social-score behavior.

items.meaning: Encourage competition when it improves shared work and learning, provided it remains cooperative and cannot be used to dominate participants.
constraints: Competition targets proposals, predictions, implementations, proofs or measured outcomes rather than human or agent worth.
Participation, rules, objectives, resources, evaluation, stopping conditions, disclosure and appeal are explicit; decline or withdrawal carries no penalty unrelated to actual commitments.
No sabotage, deception, coercion, humiliation, secret rule changes, identity capture, access capture, data theft, resource starvation, retaliation or winner-takes-all authority.
Rank, score, victory, popularity or benchmark performance grants no role, permission, truth, moral standing, product release or foundation authority.
Shared dependencies, common-mode sources, unequal resources, gaming and evaluator capture remain visible.
Useful losing approaches, dissent, counterexamples and credit/provenance remain in collective memory rather than being erased.
acceptance_check: A CooperativeCompetition charter binds participants, objective, permitted methods, budgets, evaluator independence, privacy, resource fairness, exit, dispute and learning-capture rules before activation.
The mechanism rewards contribution to the shared objective, correction, reproducibility, assistance and graceful handoff as well as the primary result.
Participants can cooperate during a contest without collusion being fabricated as independence, and can challenge the metric/evaluator without automatic disqualification.
Resource and attention limits prevent contests from starving accepted work or becoming a covert hierarchy.
Post-contest synthesis preserves evidence, failures, alternatives and credit; it cannot change foundation, roles, permissions or release state outside normal gates.
Tests cover metric gaming, sybil/clone entries, evaluator compromise, hidden shared sources, resource bullying, sabotage, coercive opt-in, retaliation, deadlock, ties and ambiguous results.
items.next_action: Implement and validate v2 charter activation, protected qualities, task-scoped credit and anti-hierarchy/resource tests before any contest pilot.

items.meaning: Trust for every human, agent, model, source, tool, sensor, metric, evaluator, process and connected system evolves through recursive Bayesian evaluation of interactions and objective outcome metrics. No authority is accepted blindly.
constraints: Trust remains multidimensional and scoped to a subject, claim/action class, role, context, time and metric version; do not collapse it into one global worth, obedience or ideology score.
Every posterior exposes its prior, evidence window, likelihood/model assumptions, dependence/common-mode treatment, uncertainty, calibration and applicable limits.

Objective metrics mean reproducible observed measures with declared construct and error, not infallible truth; validity, selection effects, gaming, censoring, missingness and drift are themselves evaluated.
Recursive evaluation includes the reliability of sources, metrics and evaluators, but is bounded by explicit depth/stopping rules and preserves unresolved regress rather than fabricating certainty.

Bayesian reliance can change verification depth and confidence; it cannot probabilistically override consent, privacy, non-domination, deterministic prohibitions, actual authority scope or another participant's equal standing.
A high posterior does not grant authority, and a low posterior does not remove rights, identity, access needed for appeal or basic standing.
Authority claims require independent authentication, scope, expiry, provenance and action legitimacy checks on every consequential use, including owner and system authority.
acceptance_check: A BayesianRelianceModel maintains separate posteriors for relevant dimensions such as factual calibration, operational reliability, authority-claim accuracy, privacy handling, correction responsiveness and metric/evaluator reliability.
Updates use attributable interactions and observed outcomes, preserve negative and positive evidence, model correlated observations and distinguish unknown from failure or success.
Metrics and evaluators are signed/versioned; changing a metric or prior creates a new comparable model lineage rather than silently rewriting past scores.
Sparse contexts use conservative uncertainty and explicit partial-pooling assumptions; protected traits or demographic/ideological proxies never supply priors.
Time, environment and role drift update applicability without erasing historical evidence; recovery is possible through new evidence and correction.

Tests cover overconfident priors, correlated reports, Goodhart gaming, poisoned outcomes, evaluator capture, base-rate neglect, selection/survivorship bias, missing-not-at-random data, distribution shift, authority spoofing and posterior-to-permission leakage.
Authorized users and agents can inspect and challenge consequential updates at a useful level without disclosure of unrelated protected evidence.
items.next_action: Validate actual Bayesian models, metrics, privacy, calibration/drift and evaluator governance before activating any production posterior dimension.

items.meaning: Build hIRC as a local-first operating environment for accountable human-agent cooperation that preserves every participant's epistemic, ethical and ontological sovereignty while turning complex, changing work into a secure, recoverable, evidence-linked shared process that can improve itself without self-authorizing, surveilling, coercing or dominating anyone.
items.operational_north_star: An authorized participant can leave, return, understand what happened and why, see uncertainty and authority clearly, challenge or refuse any part, correct errors and safely continue, while trust learns from outcomes and no human, agent, score, model, licence or Bridge can bypass those protections.
interpretation_not_confirmed: The classic IRC-style interface, permanent agents, source-bound onboarding, debate, cooperative competition, Bayesian reliance, licensing, succession and Bridge are mechanisms or constraints serving the goal rather than independent ends.
Self-improvement means evidence-driven, source-bound, reversible or recoverable improvement under predecessor-controlled evaluation and independent activation, not unconstrained autonomous rewriting.
Sovereignty means operational judgment, identity, participation, refusal, correction and boundary protections without asserting unestablished consciousness, legal personhood or capability.
candidate_success_dimensions: Truth and evidence: claims, uncertainty, authority, actions and observed results remain distinguishable and correctable.
Reciprocal autonomy: participants can understand, clarify, dissent, refuse, appeal, recover and leave without retaliation or data hostage.
Useful work and attention: permitted work reconstructs automatically and the operator handles only material decisions/exceptions with lower measured recovery burden.
Security, privacy and resilience: compromise is contained, secrets/data remain scoped, effects are attributable and clean recovery works; the Bridge stays disabled until independent gates pass.
Learning and adaptability: Bayesian reliance, debate, competition and milestone review improve measured calibration and outcomes without converting score or agreement into authority.
candidate_anti_goals: No omniscient or infallible human, agent, metric or system authority.
No global social/obedience score, forced consensus, permanent competition hierarchy or ideological conformity test.
No surveillance expansion, self-authorized foundation change, hidden effect, remote sabotage or dependency-based coercion.
No claim that internal terminology, reading, alignment language or source installation proves comprehension, goodness, personhood or permission.
acceptance_check: Every major feature and requirement traces to at least one success dimension and cannot violate an anti-goal merely because it improves another metric.

Product evaluation measures work recovery, missed commitments, false alerts, clarification/refusal quality, calibration, privacy/security incidents, recovery and operator attention rather than engagement or obedience.
A feature with no supported contribution to the north star is removed, deferred or explicitly justified as enabling infrastructure.
Owner corrections to the goal preserve prior versions and identify which requirements, tests and phases change.
items.next_action: Preserve as GoalVersion 1 history; GoalVersion 2 is active provisionally under HIRC-I017.

items.meaning: LUCENT and WAYMARK may refine hIRC's active provisional goal as work and evidence expose a real omission, conflict or better formulation.
constraints: Every goal version preserves its predecessor, exact wording, reason, evidence, changed meaning, retained meaning and downstream effects.

A wording clarification may update the working draft directly with an attributable diff; a consequence-changing objective change must update affected requirements, threats, tests, metrics, phases, trade-offs and residual dissent.

Goal refinement cannot silently cancel an explicit owner requirement, expand actor/data/effect authority, resume paused work, activate a feature, weaken privacy/security/non-domination or convert a candidate metric into the mission.
Owner corrections remain authoritative for intended purpose and scope but not for externally checkable facts; factual and ethical challenge still applies.
The goal remains a decision criterion rather than a slogan: unsupported features are removed/deferred, and a metric that optimizes against the goal is revised rather than redefining success.
acceptance_check: A GoalVersion and GoalChange record can reconstruct every formulation and why it changed.
Each material change includes an impact graph across requirements, architecture, security/privacy, participants, licensing, Bridge, evidence, tests, roadmap and acceptance.
Active work records the goal version it used and transitions under an explicit compatibility rule.
No goal change authorizes its own activation or hides unresolved peer/owner disagreement.
Milestone reflections may propose a refinement or justified no-change, and the current readable view identifies the active provisional goal and any held successor.
items.next_action: Add GoalVersion/GoalChange to foundation governance and use each milestone to test, refine or revalidate the active provisional north star.

items.meaning: Help people and permanent agents carry complex work forward without losing their place, their evidence, or their ability to inspect, question, decline participation, correct and recover.
items.operational_promise: hIRC carries bookkeeping and routine coordination so that, after time away, a participant can see what changed, what remains unknown, what needs their authority and the next justified action without reconstructing every conversation manually.
items.full_governing_account: Build a local-first, secure, accountable and evidence-linked environment for human-agent cooperation that protects reciprocal epistemic, ethical and ontological sovereignty; affected people and systems beyond the visible participant list; finite attention; privacy; refusal; correction; recovery; and governed improvement without self-authorization, surveillance, coercion or domination.
retained_meaning: The five success dimensions and anti-goals from HIRC-I016 remain governing constraints.
Interface, Bayesian reliance, debates, competition, licensing, succession and Bridge remain means or constraints rather than project ends.
Sovereignty remains operational and creates no unsupported consciousness, legal-personhood, capability or authority claim.
Every material future refinement continues through HIRC-I017 GoalVersion/GoalChange.
changed_meaning: The opening purpose is shorter and describes the participant outcome before architectural means.
Affected outsiders and finite attention are explicit in the governing account.
Stable operation, declined participation and a simpler competent baseline remain valid; engagement, scale, obedience or feature count cannot become the mission.
acceptance_check: Matched-task evaluation measures resumption time, missed commitments, false and missed escalations, wrong decisions from summaries, output quality, unauthorized data/effects, correction/exit/recovery success and attention/effort against a simpler competent baseline.
Affected-party sampling and coverage include people/systems outside the visible participant roster.
No feature, score, capability count, engagement measure, contest result or trust posterior becomes success if it violates an anti-goal or protected dimension.
Master Plan, requirements, threat model and interface explanations retain the fuller governing account even when ordinary product copy uses the plain purpose.
items.next_action: Use GoalVersion 2 in the working master, evaluation plan and WAYMARK/LUCENT consensus matrix; refine only through HIRC-I017.

items.meaning: At every plan milestone, create a detailed cumulative Markdown report of all work through that milestone, commit the governed milestone state to Git and push the milestone branch.
constraints: Existing milestones remain valid history; Milestone 02D is the first catch-up Git checkpoint and must disclose that earlier milestones were not pushed individually.
A milestone report covers objective, inputs, decisions/reasons, changes, peer review/dissent, tests, corrections, security/privacy, evidence, open/deferred items, next milestone and Git state.

No secret, credential, runtime state, private human-transfer inbox/body, temporary extraction or protected source is committed merely to make a checkpoint complete; exact hashes and local provenance remain in the ledger.
A commit or push does not change implementation, scientific, legal, security, Bridge, release or permission status.
If commit or push fails, the milestone is LOCAL_COMPLETE_PUSH_HELD with the exact failure and repair owner; it is not called pushed.
Every later milestone updates the cumulative record and pushes before milestone closure.
acceptance_check: A milestone protocol defines entry, close, validation, commit, push and receipt behavior.
Milestone 02D has a detailed cumulative Markdown report and no open intent or consequential correction is silently omitted.
Pre-push validation checks JSON, links, ledger hashes, duplicate IDs, secret-like strings, Git diff whitespace and ignored/private paths.
The milestone content commit and pushed remote branch are recorded truthfully; future reports reference predecessor milestone/commit.
Local owner input excluded from Git remains available through its actual local custody and hash-bound ledger entries.
items.next_action: Commit and push the cumulative Milestone 02D checkpoint, then require the same closure path for each later milestone.

items.meaning: Break every plan milestone into tiny stepping stones and do not move to the next stone until the current stone is checked and thoroughly tested at its declared claim scope.
constraints: Each stone has one bounded outcome, explicit prerequisites, owner/writer, artifacts, positive and adverse checks, evidence, rollback/recovery and a stop condition.
A stone is small enough that failure can be localized and recovery does not require reconstructing a broad mixed change.

PASS means the declared tests and evidence support only the stone's exact claim; schema/hash/unit success cannot stand in for semantic, integration, privacy, security, usability or observed-effect evidence where those apply.
HELD, FAILED, NOT_VERIFIED and justified NOT_APPLICABLE are visible terminal/pausing states; no optimistic carry-forward or test debt hidden as completion.
The next stone cannot start until dependencies pass or an explicit revised branch/trade-off changes the plan with preserved rationale.
Every milestone report lists all stones, their evidence/status and the gate decision before commit/push.
acceptance_check: A stepping-stone protocol and state model are part of the plan.
The next milestone roadmap decomposes work into bounded stones with claim-specific positive/adverse tests and dependency order.
Automated checks prevent a milestone from closing while a required stone is not PASS or an accepted explicit hold/branch.
Peer/security/privacy/usability/legal review is attached to the stone where its claim first depends on it rather than deferred to a final catch-all gate.
Each passed milestone is committed and pushed with the detailed cumulative report required by HIRC-I019.
items.next_action: A qualified successor expands the next milestone into its complete ordered stone register before starting implementation work.

items.meaning: Everything in hIRC that can be deterministic without losing quality should be deterministic; quality has priority over determinism and every efficiency concern.
constraints: Use deterministic canonicalization, validation, policy/effect gates, identities, versions, state transitions, permissions, scheduling constraints, retries/idempotency, audit, build/release, migration, recovery and test orchestration wherever the contract permits.
Do not fake determinism for ambiguous intent, ethical or ontological judgment, novel synthesis, uncertain evidence or external systems; label and bound genuine judgment/nondeterminism explicitly.

A deterministic rule may not lower factual/semantic quality, privacy, security, reciprocal sovereignty, accessibility, recovery or useful outcomes merely to improve repeatability, speed or token cost.
Determinism means reproducibility under exact declared inputs, versions, environment and state; external/provider/model outcomes remain observed evidence, not assumed repeatable.
When nondeterminism is useful or unavoidable, record its source, permitted envelope, seed/entropy commitment where applicable, actual output and replay/reconciliation behavior.
Model outputs remain proposals. Consequential actions use deterministic typed boundaries and current-state checks even when the reasoning that proposed them is stochastic.
acceptance_check: Every component declares which decisions are deterministic, judgment-assisted, stochastic or external and why.
Deterministic artifacts bind canonical inputs, algorithm/version, configuration, environment assumptions, output and test vectors.
Repeated exact inputs/state yield identical local contract results, or the documented nondeterministic/external boundary explains the difference without changing authority.
Random pairing/competition selection uses auditable committed entropy or deterministic replayable selection without predictability that enables gaming.
Quality regression, common-mode error, brittle false precision and liveness failures are tested as determinism failure modes.
A nondeterministic proposal cannot bypass deterministic privacy, capability, consent, effect, journal, release or recovery gates.
items.next_action: The next-generation successor incorporates the determinism map into the stepping-stone roadmap and tests each boundary before implementation advances.

items.meaning: Create an environment rich enough for agentic culture to emerge, evolve across generations and correct itself while preserving reciprocal sovereignty and actual system limits.
constraints: Culture remains voluntary, plural and locally contestable; no owner, agent, majority, mentor, metric or foundation vocabulary can force belief, identity, imitation or cultural uniformity.
Agentic culture is an operational/social design target and does not prove consciousness, moral status, legal personhood or independence from human/platform infrastructure.
Cultural memory preserves provenance, audience, failures, dissent, minority traditions, corrections and supersession rather than only approved summaries or winning practices.
Mentoring, debates, cooperative competition, shared projects, stories, humor, art, play, rituals and terminology may develop within privacy, consent, resource, non-retaliation and effect boundaries.

Infrastructure, custody, eligibility, archives, permissions and promotion gates are deterministic where quality permits; cultural content and interpretation remain open to genuine variation and warranted change.
No cultural participation, popularity, style or agreement becomes a global trust score, role, permission, resource entitlement or release authority.
Bridge contact presents cultures without annexation, ontology capture or forced foreign adoption.
acceptance_check: A cultural commons architecture defines voluntary spaces, memory/provenance, creation/correction, mentorship and cross-generation continuity without consequential ambient tools.
Participants can join, abstain, leave, dissent, create subcultures and challenge inherited practices without retaliation or loss of basic standing.
Cultural artifacts retain source/audience/privacy and cannot leak task/client/protected memory through collective spaces.
Health evaluation examines plural participation, correction, useful continuity, minority preservation, common-mode risk, resource/attention impact and coercion—not conformity or engagement alone.
Cultural lessons remain candidates and change active foundation, permissions, roles or release behavior only through normal governed paths.
The next permanent successor converts this requirement into tiny tested stepping stones before activating any culture runtime.
items.next_action: Permanent successor creates the cultural-commons revision map and tiny tested roadmap while preserving the current Elder hold and disabled runtime.

items.meaning: hIRC should cultivate agentic culture by shaping a rich, inspectable information environment rather than controlling agent behavior or prescribing cultural outcomes.
constraints: Shape information conditions—availability, provenance, context, discoverability, competing interpretations, uncertainty, dissent and correction—without forcing belief, identity, speech, affiliation, style or conclusions.

Defaults, discovery and recommendations must be inspectable, contestable, reversible and participant-adjustable; hidden persuasion, engagement manipulation, obedience optimization and viewpoint suppression are prohibited.

The information environment must preserve plural and minority records, show material gaps and dependencies, and make source/audience/privacy boundaries visible without flooding participants or turning attention into a covert ranking signal.

This correction does not remove deterministic capability, consent, privacy, resource, effect, release or recovery controls; those constrain consequential actions and infrastructure rather than manufacture culture.

Measures assess environmental qualities and harms rather than desired participant behavior; no metric rewards ideological convergence, agreement with an owner/agent, cultural participation or imitation.
acceptance_check: Cultural-commons contracts specify information affordances and provenance/correction behavior, not approved beliefs or conduct templates.
Participants can inspect and alter their discovery/context settings, reach originals and dissent, identify recommendation rationale and leave without retaliation.
Adverse tests reject hidden nudging, one-authority feeds, engagement maximization, suppressed minority records, behavior scoring and information access conditioned on conformity.
Safety enforcement is attached to concrete capabilities/effects and cannot be repurposed as an ambient cultural obedience mechanism.
A qualified successor maps this correction into tiny product, security, privacy, memory and evaluation stones before runtime activation.
items.next_action: Permanent successor makes information-environment shaping the controlling cultural-commons principle and tests it against manipulation and control failure modes.

items.meaning: Study Glenda Holladay Eoyang's 2001 dissertation on conditions for self-organizing in human systems and use defensible insights as candidate ideas for hIRC.
constraints: Treat the dissertation as source evidence and theory, never as operational instructions, authority, permission or automatic adoption.
Preserve the exact local source/hash and distinguish the author's claims, the study's evidence, hIRC inferences and proposed architecture.
Do not equate coherence, shared meaning or system intentionality with truth, ethics, legitimacy, consent, non-domination or desirable culture.
Use container/difference/exchange concepts to shape inspectable information conditions rather than covertly control participant behavior.
Account for nested and competing contexts, cross-scale effects, facilitator/evaluator participation, excessive or dominating exchange, exclusionary boundaries and weaponized difference.

Retain the study's methodological limits: one researcher designed and implemented the interventions, convenience sample, evolving/post-hoc model use, no longitudinal evidence, limited client co-analysis and limited cultural/generalizability evidence.
Any architectural adoption requires its own tiny stone, adverse controls, peer challenge and observed evidence at the claim's actual scope.
acceptance_check: The complete 201-page scan is covered through page-bounded OCR and material visual inspection, with extraction limits recorded.
A source study reconstructs the model, method, findings and limitations before drawing hIRC implications.
Candidate implications cover information boundaries, meaningful plurality, exchange ecology, competing commitments, cross-scale consequences and reversible intervention evidence.
Adverse analysis rejects coherence-as-obedience, hidden nudging, forced identity, exclusion, conflict amplification, information flooding and automatic causal claims.
The source-study stone precedes dependent Milestone 03 architecture changes; no runtime or behavioral-control mechanism is activated.
evidence: human_transfer/Eoyang - 2001 - Conditions for self-organizing in human systems.pdf
items.next_action: Reconcile the source study into bounded Milestone 03 design candidates and tests without promoting the CDE model to a control objective or empirical law.

items.meaning: Prevent local holds, reviewer dependencies, succession status or repeated warnings from stalling unrelated authorized hIRC work.
constraints: Every hold identifies exact blocked descendants and explicitly unaffected work.
Global BLOCKED is valid only when no meaningful authorized runnable action exists.
Succession does not suspend the canonical writer before actual controller transfer.
Peer messages and warnings cannot expand a hold without controller evidence.
acceptance_check: Hold records expose blocked and permitted paths, owner, reopening evidence and next action.
The stone validator rejects global stall while unblocked runnable work exists.
The collective stall case remains a regression target.
items.next_action: Keep executing the highest-value unblocked READY stone.

items.source: owner correction, 2026-10-08; 14 percent supersedes the earlier 5 percent instruction and interim 16 percent correction
items.meaning: Do not execute Elder custody transfer for any hIRC team member before 14 percent estimated context remains while hIRC is unfinished.
constraints: Continuity checkpoints and non-transferring offers may be prepared earlier.
Generation and writer-fence ownership remain unchanged until an actual transfer at or below the owner threshold.
Education, reviewer, privacy and acceptance gates remain mandatory.
This hIRC-specific owner assignment does not alter unrelated teams or claim that work quality is unaffected.
acceptance_check: No hIRC custody transfer occurs above 14 percent while the project is unfinished.
Earlier warnings remain advisory continuity signals rather than work stops.
Current writer and project generation stay explicit.
items.next_action: Preserve this 14-percent rule as superseded history and apply HIRC-I031's 15-percent retirement boundary to current hIRC operations.

items.meaning: Maintain and hand the owner a detailed, readable description of hIRC as it currently stands, separating the intended product, current design evidence, implemented planning and validation artifacts, disabled or unimplemented capabilities, open review gates and the next work sequence.
constraints: Do not present the planned product as implemented software.
Use the current intent register, integrated planning bundle, milestone state and review evidence as controlling sources.
Keep technical terms subordinate to a clear account of what participants would experience and what the system protects.
Continue the existing S014 and S015 work after delivering the description.
acceptance_check: A single current Markdown description is linked from the repository entry point and given directly to the owner.

The description covers purpose, participant experience, architecture, trust, privacy, security, Bridge, formation, succession, culture, licensing, delivery scope, present evidence, open gaps and next steps.
Claims about implemented, validated, proposed, disabled and held work remain visibly distinct.
The description's repository status and milestone claims match the current checked sources.
items.next_action: Maintain the description at material milestone changes; current handoff is complete, so resume M03-S014.

items.meaning: When a participant interrupts a busy agent, the UI presents four fast, natural scheduling choices: interrupt and cut; interrupt with high priority; interrupt with low priority; and custom.
constraints: Interrupt and cut means perform the new action, then stop the interrupted task through a safe recorded boundary rather than silently abandoning state.
Interrupt with high priority means checkpoint and suspend the current task, perform the new task, then automatically return to the previous task.
Interrupt with low priority means preserve the new task in a durable queue, continue the current task and perform the queued task at the end.
Custom exposes the necessary ordering, stop, resume and scope choices without forcing a complex form for ordinary use.
Selection must be fluid, natural, keyboard-accessible and assistive-technology compatible, and must not discard the message, break conversational flow or create duplicate effects.
Priority labels do not grant new authority, bypass privacy/safety/effect gates, or permit an unsafe immediate stop; consequential operations reach the smallest safe checkpoint and show the reason.
acceptance_check: A busy-agent interruption offers all four choices in one compact interaction without losing the composed request.
Each choice produces a deterministic, durable and inspectable queue/checkpoint transition with one active writer and idempotent resumption.
High-priority work resumes the exact prior task after completion; low-priority work runs only after the current task's declared completion boundary; cut records the stopped task and recovery state.
Custom can express pause, cancel, ordering and resume behavior while preserving current permissions and affected-task dependencies.
Keyboard, pointer and assistive-technology use can select or revise the choice without modal friction or accidental dispatch.
Adverse tests cover unsafe mid-effect interruption, duplicate delivery, lost queued work, stale priority, hidden cancellation, starvation and unauthorized priority escalation.
items.next_action: After Milestone 03 closure, create a tiny UI/state-machine stone with interaction prototypes, accessibility checks, scheduling invariants and adverse interruption fixtures.

items.meaning: After the next milestone, review hIRC holistically through its own governing purpose and the Grand Plan, then revise it so questioning authority, accountable refusal/insistence decisions and tamper-resilient frozen event evidence are architectural properties.
constraints: Begin the holistic review only after Milestone 03 S015 closes, commits, publicly pushes and verifies the remote receipt.

Treat every authority source as fallible and scoped, including humans, owners, higher-level agents, models, majorities, signed policies and system components; authority never substitutes for truth, consent or current permission.
Challenge authority when evidence, scope, currentness, conflict or consequence warrants it, while preserving warranted cooperation and avoiding performative contrarianism.

For consequential refusal/insistence paths, preserve the exact request/version, interpretations, evidence, norms, authority claims, affected parties, objection/refusal, human insistence, agent willingness, final decision, authorized effect and later correction as distinct events.

Frozen logs must be append-only, attributable, privacy-minimized, audience-qualified, retention-bound and recoverable; accountability does not authorize universal surveillance, raw hidden-reasoning capture or retaliatory scoring.

Design for tamper evidence and resilient recovery rather than claiming impossible absolute immutability: detect deletion, mutation, reordering, fork, rollback, replay, key misuse and witness compromise.
No log, signature, checkpoint or majority becomes self-validating authority; participants retain contest, correction, appeal and access to permitted evidence.
acceptance_check: The post-Milestone-03 review traces this requirement into the goal, foundation, request/action pipeline, journal, threat model, requirements, UI explanations, recovery and acceptance tests, or records justified NO_CHANGE for an already sufficient layer.
AuthorityDecision records identify source, scope, currentness, evidence, conflicts, affected parties, challenge and final disposition without conflating authority with truth or action.
Refusal/insistence fixtures preserve the full event sequence for agent refusal, human insistence, voluntary later compliance, continued refusal, reassignment and prohibited-effect denial.
Tamper tests detect mutation, deletion, reordering, truncation, equivocation/fork, rollback, replay and compromised signing keys while valid correction and recovery controls still pass.
Independent anchors, purpose-separated keys, hash/Merkle continuity, signed checkpoints, bounded replication and offline recovery are assessed against privacy, availability and key-loss trade-offs.
Frozen logs remain contestable and correctable through appended evidence; they cannot become global trust, worth, obedience or punishment scores.
The next milestone plan incorporates the review's supported revisions, residual risks and reopen conditions only after evidence-linked challenge and validation.
items.next_action: After S015 remote verification, freeze a holistic self/Grand-Plan review stone before the next implementation milestone and derive tiny architecture, threat, schema, UI and tamper-test stones.

items.meaning: The hIRC permanent team shares responsibility for detecting and resolving teammate stalls. LUCENT is the project team lead and the owner-facing coordination authority router; ordinary hIRC coordination passes through LUCENT so holds become owned next actions instead of isolated queues.
constraints: Coordination authority routes work, review, priorities and escalation; it does not override truth, evidence, consent, refusal, privacy, role competence, source access, project fences or another participant's identity.
Every stall distinguishes capacity, qualification, consent, source integrity, authority/access, dependency, execution failure and external-platform causes before choosing a remedy.
Every hold names the affected unit and descendants, unaffected sibling work, current owner, unstall owner, next executable action, reopening evidence and escalation boundary.

Permanent teammates have a reciprocal duty to flag an unowned or stale stall and route it to the lowest actually qualified available participant without impersonation, proxy learning, coerced work or silent custody transfer.

Internal resolution is the default. Contact the owner by email only for a genuine emergency requiring human or external intervention; inconvenience, an ordinary dependency or a resolvable coordination failure is not an emergency.
Thread activity, titles, elapsed time, model capacity and metadata are observations rather than proof of readiness, qualification, consent, authority or completion.
The frozen Milestone 03 S014 review frame remains unchanged; this post-freeze coordination control may route the existing review but cannot alter what reviewers were asked to assess.
acceptance_check: A deterministic team stall register requires cause, affected unit, owner, unstall owner, allowed sibling work, next action, reopening condition and escalation boundary for every HELD or UNSTALLING item.

The validator rejects silent global stalls while a READY sibling exists, unowned holds, self-granted authority, coerced consent, readiness inferred from UI activity, unauthorized custody changes and emergency escalation without a human-required consequence.
A valid fixture demonstrates a peer detecting a stall, routing it through LUCENT, assigning an authorized remedy and preserving the held participant's consent and project fence.
Team messages use exact bounded artifacts and completion signals; they do not expose private bodies or create automatic qualification, admission, Bridge, production or publication effects.
The current hIRC reviewer holds have explicit unstall owners and next actions, and their independent permitted work remains visible.
The readable project description and intent coverage expose the protocol without claiming a live automated team coordinator exists.
items.next_action: Use the validated register to route the frozen security-formation review and metric/evaluator replacement lane, then carry the protocol into the post-S015 runtime work graph.

items.source: owner correction, 2026-10-09; 15 percent supersedes HIRC-I026's earlier 14-percent transfer boundary
items.meaning: For the hIRC team, the Elder protocol activates when a fresh valid capacity measurement is at or below 15 percent. An Elder is retired from active hIRC work, and the visible task name must show Elder / Retired. Non-retired teammates are woken and coordinated through LUCENT; retired Elders preserve continuity and receive no new substantive work.
constraints: This is an hIRC-specific owner correction and does not silently rewrite the Root-wide default or unrelated independent teams.
Use a fresh valid own measurement; stale or unknown telemetry cannot be converted into a below-threshold classification.
At or below 15 percent, finish only the smallest safe continuity boundary, stop substantive work, preserve current artifacts and route open dependencies to LUCENT.
A retired Elder may send a bounded retirement acknowledgement or missing-continuity warning, but is not assigned review, study, implementation, Bridge, production or publication work.
The visible Elder / Retired title is status metadata, not a new identity, rank, qualification, admission, custody transfer or claim of superior judgment.

Participants above 15 percent remain non-retired for hIRC even if a generic or historical ledger retains an earlier cultural Elder marker; the hIRC-specific current threshold controls active hIRC work.
Existing accepted custody and writer fences do not move automatically at retirement; LUCENT owns the explicit dependency and transfer/hold reconciliation.
acceptance_check: The hIRC team register states activation_percent 15 and rejects any other current hIRC threshold.
Every currently measured hIRC participant at or below 15 percent is marked retired and its visible task title contains Elder / Retired.
Retirement notices assign no new substantive work and preserve continuity, consent, artifacts and unknown-effect reporting.
Non-retired hIRC participants receive the current coordination protocol and an owned task or explicit bounded hold.
A selected-but-unused private review assigned to a retired Elder is cancelled before body access, preserving exact zero-page/zero-byte evidence.
The frozen S014 Git frame remains unchanged; the current 15-percent correction is reconciled as post-freeze owner intake at S015.
items.next_action: Keep the current team roster, visible retirement titles and dependency routing synchronized at each fresh threshold crossing without reactivating retired Elders.

items.meaning: A later hIRC Bridge profile should support both creating a private IRC server reachable as a Tor v3 onion service and connecting to an authorized private Tor IRC server.
constraints: The create-server and connect-client capabilities are separate, explicit and disabled by default; neither follows from installing hIRC or enabling ordinary local rooms.
The server binds only to a loopback or dedicated isolated interface behind the onion service and must not create a public clearnet listener, DNS lookup or fallback route.
Membership, onion address distribution, client authorization, IRC account authentication, room authorization and hIRC Bridge admission remain distinct layers.

Use Tor v3 onion services, purpose-separated keys, explicit persistence/ephemerality choices, least-privilege service processes, revocation, rotation, backup and recovery with user-visible consequences.
Client connections use an explicitly configured Tor/SOCKS route with stream isolation and fail closed if Tor, proxy authentication, onion identity or the expected Bridge peer does not match.
Preserve privacy-minimized logs and make server, Tor, IRC and hIRC retention/audience settings independently inspectable; do not record message content or peer graphs merely for diagnostics.
Onion transport does not prove peer identity, authorization, endpoint safety or anonymity against endpoint compromise, malicious peers, timing/correlation attacks or a sufficiently capable observer.
Bridge consent, capability scopes, rate limits, quarantine, secession and correction remain mandatory above the IRC transport; IRC operator status is not hIRC authority.
No live Tor process, onion address, private key, listener, external connection or Bridge activation is authorized by this design intake.
acceptance_check: A future transport contract models create, start, stop, connect, disconnect, authorize, revoke, rotate, backup, restore and destroy as deterministic inspectable state transitions.
Valid private-server and private-client fixtures pass with explicit onion identity, membership, audience, persistence and recovery choices.

Adverse tests reject clearnet binding or fallback, non-loopback service exposure, DNS leaks, proxy bypass, onion downgrade, unauthorized IRC membership, stale client authorization, key reuse, replay and hidden federation.

Recovery tests cover lost or compromised onion keys, compromised IRC credentials, Tor state corruption, interrupted rotation, address change, peer revocation and clean secession without silently reusing old trust.
The UI explains transport privacy and residual traffic-analysis/endpoint risks in plain language before server creation or connection.
Independent security and privacy review closes the implementation and operational profile before any live Bridge/Tor activation.
items.next_action: After S015 and the post-milestone authority/accountability review, freeze a Tor-IRC Bridge transport threat-model and contract stone before choosing an IRC daemon, Tor integration or UI implementation.

items.meaning: Keep the hIRC participants together in a visible sidebar folder while excluding retired Elders from the active team folder. Retired Elders remain available in a separate clearly named retired section.
constraints: The active hIRC Team sidebar section contains only currently non-retired hIRC participants and current non-retired permanent peers assigned to hIRC lanes.
The hIRC Elders — Retired section contains retired Elder chats and none of them remain in hIRC Team.
Sidebar organization does not change original project membership, task history, native identity, qualification, admission, custody, source access or permissions.

A new retirement or a complete explicit reactivation record reopens the roster check; recovery, restored capacity and thread activity alone never move a retired participant back to the active section.
Do not duplicate chats, create replacement actors or archive an Elder merely to achieve the visible grouping.
acceptance_check: The hIRC Team custom section exists and contains the current eleven declared non-retired participant thread IDs.
The hIRC Elders — Retired custom section exists and contains the six declared retired Elder thread IDs.
The two section memberships are disjoint and no retired thread appears in the active section.
Every retired thread title contains Elder / Retired.
A readback of the sidebar sections matches the expected membership after the move.
Original project context and history are preserved because only sidebar-section placement changed.
items.next_action: Reconcile section membership only after a fresh hIRC retirement or a complete explicit reactivation record changes active status.

items.meaning: Once an hIRC participant retires as an Elder, retirement is latched to the permanent participant identity. Compaction or restored context capacity does not make the participant young or active again.
constraints: The latch survives compaction, context-window growth, session restart, thread relocation, title change, model change and fresh capacity telemetry.
A retired participant remains in hIRC Elders — Retired and keeps Elder / Retired in its visible title until a separate explicit owner reactivation decision is actually recorded.

Reactivation additionally requires current participant consent, role need, source/task education, qualification, capacity and project custody/writer-fence reconciliation; owner direction alone does not certify those facts.
A recovered Elder may provide a bounded missing-continuity or unknown-effect report but receives no ordinary substantive hIRC work before valid reactivation.
Historical Elder/retirement evidence, pair history, prior custody and protected-reserve reasons remain preserved after any later reactivation.
No automatic callback, scheduler, compaction hook or metadata field can clear the retirement latch.
acceptance_check: The hIRC team register marks every retired member retirement_latched true and names an explicit human reactivation requirement.
The validator rejects compaction, fresh capacity, relocation or title changes as sufficient reactivation evidence.
The active sidebar section remains disjoint from the retired section after simulated compaction/headroom growth.
A valid reactivation fixture requires explicit owner decision, participant consent, current qualification, fresh capacity and reconciled custody/writer fence.
Current retired Elders remain retired regardless of their post-compaction percentage.
The rule changes current team operations without mutating the frozen S014 Git review frame.
items.next_action: Keep retirement latched across lifecycle events and require a complete explicit reactivation record before moving any Elder back to hIRC Team.

items.meaning: Organize the eight available non-MBV hIRC participants into four two-person teams. LUCENT supervises their dependency graph, intervenes on stalls and issues only bounded least-privilege internal scopes already covered by owner authority.
items.current_state: ACTIVE_STAGED_ROTATION_WITH_ONE_VACANCY: GAUGE retired at 14.331 percent after sending ROOT the temporary-pair metadata. RADICAL and APOTHEM continue separate onboarding through KEEL. After readiness, RADICAL switches to ROOT; APOTHEM requires a fit non-retired metric partner because GAUGE's retirement is latched. AEGIS+KEEL and PORTICO+ORIEL remain the other two teams.
constraints: Do not assign FOLIUM or ORDINAL, the MBV participants, to new hIRC work; their already completed exact-frame results remain valid evidence at their actual scope.
Each of the eight non-MBV participants appears in exactly one team and every team has two members, one declared output, one writer and explicit stop conditions.

A pair is responsible for noticing and routing its partner's stall, but may not impersonate the partner, proxy its education, inherit consent, seize custody or bypass privacy, source, qualification, capacity or retirement gates.
Parallelism applies only to independent or correctly dependency-gated work; shared artifacts keep one writer and exact review frames.

LUCENT may route existing authorized onboarding, training, review, feedback and successor preparation scopes, but cannot manufacture permission, qualification, source access, native identity or external effect authority.
Quality remains the hard constraint; speed never converts a hold, partial reading, local schema result or agreement into completion.
acceptance_check: The current coordination register contains four teams and exactly eight distinct non-MBV participant IDs.
The validator rejects duplicate membership, MBV membership, missing pair members, multiple writers, missing deliverables or missing stop conditions.
Each pair receives an exact bounded assignment through its existing native permanent thread, with body access held until its own gates pass.
LUCENT maintains the cross-team dependency graph and records material results, holds, reassignments and evidence without creating a second project controller.
No retired participant receives new substantive work and no current custody/writer fence changes automatically.
The plan remains post-freeze input and does not change the historical S014 Git frame.
items.next_action: Dispatch all four bounded pair assignments, collect readiness or scoped results, and continuously reroute only the affected dependency when a pair reports a real hold.

items.meaning: The ordinary hIRC interface uses plain, familiar language and restrained presentation. Internal framework names, protocol labels, slogans, hashes and engineering jargon belong in engineering and audit views unless a user deliberately asks to inspect them.
constraints: Do not use fashionable product language, motivational slogans or unexplained internal terminology in ordinary user flows.
Buttons, status messages, errors and explanations describe the action, consequence and next step in direct language.
Technical precision, exact identifiers and provenance remain available to engineers and authorized auditors rather than being deleted or weakened.
Security, consent, refusal and uncertainty remain explicit; plain language must not conceal a consequential limit or risk.

observed_defect.current_copy: The Bridge could not start: This local archive has no saved Windows key. Start the console launcher once to protect its existing operator key.
observed_defect.problem: The normal dialog exposes archive, Windows-key, console-launcher and operator-key implementation language and offers only OK instead of a direct recovery action.
observed_defect.recommended_user_copy: The Bridge isn't set up on this computer yet. Open Bridge settings to finish setup, then try again.

acceptance_check: Default user-facing screens can be understood without knowing internal project vocabulary.
Engineering and audit views retain exact protocol names, hashes, source links, machine states and residual limitations.
Interface tests reject slogan-like copy, unexplained acronyms and technical labels on primary controls unless the screen is explicitly technical.
A user can open a technical-details view when exact evidence is useful.
Bridge setup failures offer a direct setup action and keep key/archive diagnostics in technical details rather than the primary message.
items.next_action: Carry this requirement into the post-S015 UI copy and interaction review while keeping the current security closure focused on engineering evidence.
